note: General agronomic reference compiled by the Field Verse SE team for the demo. Duration and tolerance values are broad typical ranges across varieties and climates — they are NOT location-specific recommendations and must be verified with local extension services and seed suppliers.

image.alt: Illustration of rice plants with drooping golden grain heads standing in shallow water

crops.description: A staple grain usually grown in flooded or very wet fields. It needs a lot of water, so it depends on reliable rain or irrigation.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Typical range across varieties; short-duration varieties exist. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a tall maize plant with a yellow cob, silk and a tassel on top

crops.description: A tall grain crop used for food and animal feed. It needs steady moisture, especially around flowering.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Highland maize can take longer than lowland maize. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a mung bean plant with clusters of thin green pods and small green beans

crops.description: A fast-growing legume with small green beans. It usually needs less water than rice and, like other legumes, works with soil bacteria to add nitrogen.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Sensitive to waterlogging. Verify variety duration locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a cowpea plant with long thin pods and pale purple flowers

crops.description: A hardy legume known for coping with heat and dry spells. Leaves and beans are eaten, and it can add nitrogen to the soil.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Grain types vs. leafy types differ in duration. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a common bean plant with flat green pods and red speckled kidney-shaped beans

crops.description: A widely eaten bean that grows well in cooler highland areas. It is sensitive to drought and very high heat during flowering.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Bush types are shorter than climbing types. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a sorghum plant with a compact reddish-brown grain head on a tall stalk

crops.description: A grain crop known for tolerating heat and dry conditions better than maize. Used for food, feed and fodder.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Cold highland sites may slow growth. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a soybean plant with fuzzy pods in clusters and pale yellow beans

crops.description: A protein-rich legume grown widely for oil and animal feed. It can form nitrogen-fixing partnerships with soil bacteria.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Maturity group strongly affects duration. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of sunn hemp with tall thin stems, narrow leaves and bright yellow flowers

crops.description: A fast-growing legume cover crop. It keeps soil covered, adds plant material, and can add nitrogen when it is turned into the soil.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Duration shown is to green-manure stage, not seed harvest. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a lablab vine with purple flowers and flat curved purple-green pods

crops.description: A vigorous climbing legume used as food, fodder and cover. It has deep roots and can keep growing into the dry season.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Grows slowly at first. Verify suitability for highland sites locally.

image.alt: Illustration of golden wheat stalks with long bearded grain heads

crops.description: A grain crop for bread and flour that grows best in cooler, drier seasons. Too much heat or rain at harvest can lower grain quality.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Spring and winter wheat differ greatly in duration. Verify locally.

image.alt: Illustration of a cassava plant with hand-shaped leaves and brown starchy roots in the soil

crops.description: A hardy root crop grown for its starchy roots. It copes with poor soils and dry spells, but stays in the field for many months.

source.name: General agronomic reference (Field Verse team)
source.note: Harvest age varies widely by variety and use (8–18 months). Verify locally.
